prompt:
Using the lesson's detector (`WINDOW = 60`, `LIMIT = 5`, alert when `len(q) > LIMIT`), one IP has failed logins at these times in seconds:

```
0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 55, 70
```

At which timestamps does `alert` fire?

options.explanation: It also fires on every later event while more than 5 events remain in the window; the detector does not suppress repeats.
At 70 seconds the cutoff is 10 seconds. Events at 0 and 10 are removed, leaving six failures; that still exceeds five.
Correct. At 50 there are 6 events in the window, at 55 there are 7, and at 70, after dropping 0 and 10, there are 6.

options.text: It never fires, because no 60-second window contains more than 5 events
options.explanation: The window 0 to 50 already contains 6 events (0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50).

workedExample:
Drop rule: remove from the front while `q[0] <= ts - 60`. So each new event keeps only events from the previous 60 seconds, excluding one exactly 60 seconds older. At 70 s the cut-off is 10 s, so the events at 0 and 10 drop out and 6 remain.

The table applies this at every event:

```
ts  cutoff  window             len
0   -60     [0]                 1
10  -50     [0,10]              2
20  -40     [0..20]             3
30  -30     [0..30]             4
40  -20     [0..40]             5
50  -10     [0..50]             6 !
55   -5     [0..55]             7 !
70   10     [20,30,40,50,55,70] 6 !
```

Alerts at 50, 55 and 70. In practice you would de-duplicate (one alert per IP per window) to avoid flooding the SOC.
